title: Show more detailed network activity, like System Monitor's Download / Upload Rate history chart
line: The Networks widget's speed graph now shows the last 80 seconds of traffic as soon as you open a connection's details, instead of starting empty.
explanation: The applet computed speeds in each connection's list delegate from NetworkManager's device statistics, which it only switched on while the popup was open; the delegates and the network model are destroyed when the popup closes, so the graph always started from nothing. A new TrafficHistory object, kept alive by the applet's root item, samples the byte counters of every activated device every 2 seconds (from /sys/class/net, so NetworkManager no longer has to poll and emit statistics) and keeps the last 40 speeds; the details graph and the speed subtitle read from it. TrafficMonitor shows a given history when one is passed and otherwise keeps its old live behaviour for the KCMs.

commits.message:
applet: keep a short speed history for the details graph

The applet only measured network speeds while its popup was open, so the
speed graph was always empty when opening a connection's details. Sample
the speed of activated devices all the time and show that history.

BUG: 514435

media.caption: Details opened after reopening the popup: the graph only has the last few seconds
Details opened right after opening the popup for the first time: the graph already shows the last 80 seconds

review.text: A small C++ history object owned by the applet root is the right shape, and reading /sys counters avoids NetworkManager's shared refresh-rate setting; the media show a full graph on first open. But it turns plasmashell into a permanent 2-second poller that also emits a property change (rebuilding two QVariantMaps and re-evaluating bindings) every tick even while the popup is closed, which reverses the deliberate 50834af82 ('stop collecting upload/download data once the popup dialog is closed') and is likely to be pushed back on for idle wakeups.
changes: Only sample and emit while it matters, or make the background part as cheap as possible: keep counters/history internally but emit updated() (and build the maps) only while the popup is expanded, e.g. via an 'active' property bound to expanded.
Explain in the MR why this background sampling is acceptable relative to 50834af82 (sysfs read, no NetworkManager D-Bus traffic, timer stops when disconnected) so the maintainers can weigh it.
